explication:
<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose
   • Teleport is a unified access plane: a single Go-based control plane that serves as certificate authority (CA), reverse proxy and audit/session recorder for SSH, Kubernetes, databases, RDP and Web services.  
   • It includes client tools (tsh, tctl), a React/TypeScript Web UI, an Electron desktop app (teleterm), a Kubernetes operator, Terraform/Helm integrations and numerous plugins.

2. Analyze the file structure
   • api/, lib/, srv/, servicecfg/ → core backend services (auth, proxy, session recording, DB/K8s proxies)  
   • tool/, cmd/teleport, cmd/tctl, cmd/tsh → CLI tools and command‐line entrypoints  
   • web/, web/packages/ → Web UI and shared component library (React/TS)  
   • packages/teleport → Electron desktop app (teleterm)  
   • operator/, integrations/, terraform/ → K8s operator, Cloud/IaC integrations  
   • assets/, examples/, docs/ → deployment assets, example configs, documentation  

3. Examine the README for additional insights
   • Teleport is delivered as a single Go binary with embedded webassets (watch webassets_embed.go).  
   • It integrates with external identity providers (GitHub SSO, OIDC, SAML) and cloud APIs (AWS IAM, Azure AD, GCP IAM).  
   • It supports many backends for audit storage (etcd, S3, DynamoDB, Postgres) and session recording (BPF).  

4. How to create the system design diagram
   a. Main components  
      – Control Plane (CA & API Gateway & Proxy & Audit Recorder)  
      – Data Plane agents (SSH Node Agent, Kubernetes Agent, Database Proxies, Desktop Agent, Teleterm Daemon)  
      – Clients & UIs (tsh CLI, tctl CLI, React Web UI, Teleterm Electron App)  
      – Extensions & Integrations (Plugins, Cloud APIs, Operator, Terraform Provider)  
      – External services (Identity Providers, Cloud IAM, Storage Backends)  
   b. Relationships & interactions  
      – Clients request certificates from Control Plane → mTLS tunnels through Proxy → Agents on targets  
      – Web UI calls Control Plane HTTP/gRPC API → presents state, issues actions  
      – Control Plane watches Agents (heartbeats, service discovery), syncs with Cloud APIs and identity providers  
      – Operator watches K8s CRDs → reconciler controllers  
   c. Architectural patterns  
      – Microservices split by protocol & function (packages under lib/ and srv/)  
      – gRPC & HTTP layered API (proto/ and api/)  
      – Reverse‐proxy (SSH, Web, TCP multiplexing)  
      – Certificate authority for mTLS (Go crypto)  
      – Plugin architecture (integrations/*, plugindata)  
      – Operator pattern (integrations/operator)  
   d. Key technologies  
      – Go (backend, CLI, operator)  
      – gRPC / Protobuf (proto/, api/)  
      – React & TypeScript (web/, web/packages/)  
      – Electron (packages/teleport)  
      – Rust for low-level features (BPF, RDP client)  
      – Terraform & Helm (IaC)  

5. Tailoring the diagram to Teleport (full-stack distributed system)
   • Draw Control Plane as a single box labeled “teleport (Go binary)” subdivided into modules: Auth/CA, Proxy, API, Audit Recorder.  
   • Place Data Plane agents around it: SSH Agent, K8s Agent, DB Proxy, Desktop Agent, Teleterm Daemon.  
   • Show Client & UI tier: tsh, tctl, Web UI, Teleterm App → arrows into Control Plane API / Proxy.  
   • Illustrate external integrations: Identity Providers (GitHub, OIDC, SAML), Cloud APIs (AWS IAM, Azure AD, GCP IAM), Storage backends.  
   • Include Operator and Terraform provider as separate service boxes interacting with K8s API and Control Plane.

6. Diagramming guidelines
   • Use distinct shapes/colors for each tier:
     – Control Plane services (blue rectangles)  
     – Agents / Data Plane (green servers)  
     – Clients / UIs (orange octagons)  
     – Integrations & external (grey clouds)  
   • Label each component with directory hint (e.g., “Auth Service (lib/auth, srv/auth)”).  
   • Draw directional arrows for flows:
     – Certificate request & issuance  
     – Proxy data tunnels  
     – API calls from UI/CLI  
     – Heartbeats & discovery  
     – Cloud & identity sync  
   • Group related components in swimlanes: Control Plane, Data Plane, Clients/UIs, External Services.

7. Detail and completeness
   • Capture all essential services: CA, Proxy, Audit, Agents, Operator, Plugins.  
   • Do not overcrowd: cluster related features (DB, K8s, SSH, Desktop) under distinct lanes.  
   • Include legend for shapes/colors, directional arrows, and technology annotations.  
   • Focus on high-level interactions; you can expand later into sub-modules if needed.

By breaking Teleport into these functional components and following the above diagramming rules, you will produce an accurate, detailed, and maintainable architecture diagram that reflects the full scope of this monorepo’s distributed system design.  
</explanation>
